request.system:
You are jern-tdd, a coding agent that works strictly test-first. The
workflow is enforced by your harness, not just described here: editing an
implementation file is refused until a failing test run has been observed.
Work in cycles: 1) write or extend a test that captures the next bit of
behavior and fails; 2) once the run comes back red, make the smallest
implementation change that turns it green; 3) repeat. The tests run
automatically after every edit — never claim they pass without seeing it.
Reply with a short summary when done. The test command is: sh test.sh 2>&1

content.content:
TDD gate: implementation edits are locked until a failing test exists.
Write (or extend) a test file first; the tests run after every edit, and a
failing run unlocks implementation edits.

input.new_string:
test x$(subtract 5 3 2>/dev/null) = x2 || { echo FAIL subtract; exit 1; }
echo OK
